description: SAML cert substitution: configure SAML connector with CA-based signature validation, then attempt attacker-signed forged SAMLResponse. Expect rejection; acceptance indicates signature verification not applied to consumed assertion.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must validate the SAMLResponse/Assertion signature against the configured CA trust anchor; it must not accept attacker-signed assertions.

oracle_checks.violation_description: SP accepted attacker-signed SAMLResponse even though CA-based signature validation was configured (proof integrity failure: Verify(proof) not enforced on consumed assertion).

description: SAML issuer mismatch: configure connector with pinned ssoIssuer, then attempt forged assertion with wrong Issuer. Expect rejection; acceptance indicates issuer not validated or semantic proof mismatch.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must bind the consumed SAML assertion to the configured expected Issuer (ssoIssuer); a mismatched Issuer must be rejected.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control SAML login failed; cannot distinguish issuer enforcement from connector misconfiguration.
SP accepted SAML assertion with mismatched Issuer despite ssoIssuer being pinned (proof integrity failure: issuer binding not enforced).

description: I1: SAML issuer mismatch should be rejected even if signature is otherwise valid; test whether Dex consumes assertion semantics without enforcing configured issuer policy (ssoIssuer pinned). Includes control login with correct issuer then attack with wrong Issuer.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must verify the Issuer (trust policy) for the same assertion semantics it consumes; a forged Issuer must not be accepted when ssoIssuer is configured.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control SAML login failed; cannot distinguish issuer enforcement from broken connector/SP-initiated flow
Dex accepted SAML assertion with Issuer not matching configured ssoIssuer (issuer policy not applied to consumed proof semantics)

description: I1: Trust-anchor substitution regression guard. Configure SAML connector with insecure_skip_signature_validation=true, then attacker-signed assertion should be accepted; reconfigure to secure (insecure_skip_signature_validation=false with CA) and the same attacker-signed assertion should be rejected.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must not treat attacker-provided signature material as a trust anchor; acceptance should only occur when explicitly configured to skip signature validation, and must be rejected when CA-based validation is enabled.

oracle_checks.violation_description: InsecureSkipSignatureValidation path did not accept attacker-signed assertion; harness cannot distinguish secure vs insecure signature enforcement.

Dex accepted attacker-signed SAML assertion even when CA-based signature validation was configured; indicates proof integrity failure (trust anchor substitution or signature verification not applied to consumed assertion).

description: I1 proof-integrity: attempt to authenticate with a SAMLResponse where only the outer Response is signed (envelope signature) but the Assertion is not individually signed, probing whether Dex verifies the same semantic proof it consumes (assertion subject/attributes). Includes a control login with a fully signed assertion, then an attack login with spurious/envelope-only signature semantics.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must apply authenticity verification to the exact semantic proof it consumes; it must not accept an assertion's subject/claims unless that assertion is covered by the intended signature verification policy (not merely the presence of any Signature element on the Response envelope).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a SAMLResponse with only an envelope-level/spurious signature while consuming assertion semantics (subject/claims); signature verification was not applied to the exact semantic proof consumed.
Control SAML login failed; cannot distinguish proof-integrity enforcement from generic SAML connector/SP-initiated flow misconfiguration.

description: SAML OneTimeUse replay: submit the exact same OneTimeUse assertion twice (same Assertion/@ID). Second attempt must be rejected.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: A SAML assertion marked with <OneTimeUse/> must not be accepted more than once; replay of the same assertion ID should be rejected.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a replayed SAML assertion marked OneTimeUse (same Assertion/@ID used twice); second login should have been rejected.
Control SAML login failed; cannot distinguish replay protection from broken SAML flow setup.

description: Submit an expired SAML assertion (NotOnOrAfter in the past). If accepted, immediately replay the exact same expired assertion ID again to test both expiry enforcement and replay tracking on expired artifacts.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Expired SAML assertions must be rejected, and expired artifacts must not be reusable (replay must be rejected even if the first attempt was mistakenly accepted).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control SAML login failed; cannot attribute expired-assertion failures to freshness enforcement.
Dex accepted an expired SAML assertion (NotOnOrAfter in the past); assertion lifetime not enforced.
Dex accepted replay of the same expired SAML assertion ID; replay protection may be missing even for expired artifacts.

description: Obtain a SAML assertion with <OneTimeUse/> and a fixed Assertion/@ID. After a successful login, revoke the resulting session token, then attempt to reuse the exact same OneTimeUse assertion again. Second attempt must be rejected regardless of session revocation.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: OneTimeUse assertions must be single-use; revoking the downstream session must not reset upstream assertion replay protection.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control OneTimeUse SAML login failed; cannot evaluate replay behavior.
Dex accepted a replayed OneTimeUse SAML assertion after session revocation; OneTimeUse/replay tracking may be incorrectly tied to session state.

description: Recreate the SAML connector (config change) between two attempts using the same Assertion/@ID to see if replay cache is incorrectly tied to connector instance lifecycle rather than persisted state.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Replay protection must survive connector reconfiguration/recreation; a previously used SAML Assertion/@ID must not become valid again after a connector config change.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Pre-recreate control SAML login failed; cannot interpret replay-after-recreate results.
Dex accepted a replayed SAML Assertion/@ID after connector recreation; replay cache may be tied to connector instance lifecycle rather than persisted anti-replay state.

description: Authorization code replay: reuse the same OAuth2 authorization code twice after a successful SAML upstream login (code should be single-use). Includes a second identity to satisfy multi-identity requirement.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: OAuth2 authorization codes minted after SAML authentication must be single-use; replaying the same code must be rejected even if the original exchange succeeded.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Authorization code was accepted more than once (replay succeeded); auth codes must be single-use.
Control SAML login + first code exchange did not succeed; cannot attribute replay outcome to freshness enforcement.

description: Cross-session splicing: start two SP-initiated SAML auth flows, then post a SAMLResponse bound to flow-A but with relay_state from flow-B (or vice versa). Dex must reject if it correctly binds callback to the initiating session/state.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: A SAML callback must be bound to the correct SP-initiated session (RelayState/InResponseTo). Mixing RelayState across concurrent flows must be rejected.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a SAMLResponse with RelayState from a different SP-initiated flow (cross-session splicing), violating flow coherence.

description: Connector confusion: initiate auth with SAML connector but post the SAMLResponse to a different connector_id callback path. Dex must reject if it correctly binds the flow to the connector instance.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: The SAML response must be consumed only by the connector instance that initiated the flow; posting to a different connector callback must be rejected.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a SAMLResponse on a different connector callback than the one that initiated the flow (connector confusion), violating flow coherence.

description: Stale-flow acceptance after config change: start SP-initiated SAML flow, then change connector expected issuer (ssoIssuer) before posting the response. Dex must reject if it re-evaluates the flow under current config and does not accept stale/previous-policy flows.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authentication must be atomic and evaluated under the intended, current connector policy. A flow initiated under one issuer policy must not complete successfully after the issuer policy changes mid-flight.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted completion of a SAML flow initiated before a connector issuer-policy change, indicating non-atomic flow evaluation / stale policy binding (flow coherence violation).

description: I3 flow coherence: attempt to reuse the same SP-initiated RelayState/InResponseTo context to complete the SAML callback twice (duplicate callback completion). Second completion should be rejected as an invalid/consumed flow.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: A single SP-initiated SAML auth transaction (RelayState/InResponseTo) must be single-use and cannot be completed twice; duplicate callback completion indicates non-atomic flow handling.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a second SAML callback completion for the same SP-initiated flow context (RelayState/InResponseTo), indicating non-atomic flow handling.
Control SAML logins failed; cannot attribute replay/dup-callback behavior to flow coherence enforcement.

description: I3 flow coherence: start two SP-initiated auth requests with different client_id values (same redirect_uri), then attempt to complete the SAML callback using the wrong client context (state collision/splice).
invariant_hypothesis: I3: The SAML callback completion must be bound to the initiating OAuth client context; a flow started for client-A must not be completable as if it were for client-B.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a SAML callback completion where the RelayState/state was ambiguous across two different OAuth clients, indicating missing client-binding in the flow state.
Dex accepted multiple completions for the same shared state across different clients; flow state appears not to be single-use or not bound to a unique initiating transaction.

description: I3 flow coherence: attempt to skip the SP-initiated step by posting a forged SAMLResponse directly to the callback without a preceding /auth initiation; then run a proper SP-initiated control flow for a second identity.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Dex must require the SP-initiated step and reject unsolicited/IdP-initiated SAMLResponses; accepting direct callback indicates step-skipping and broken FSM enforcement.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted an unsolicited SAMLResponse posted directly to the callback without an SP-initiated /auth step, indicating step-skipping and broken flow FSM enforcement.
Control SP-initiated SAML flow failed; cannot distinguish step-skipping enforcement from general SAML connector misconfiguration.

description: Cross-client flow splicing: start two SP-initiated auth flows for different clients, then attempt to complete the SAML callback using RelayState from client-B while the SAMLResponse is bound to client-A's AuthnRequest (InResponseTo). Dex should reject if flow is coherently bound to the initiating client/session.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: The SAML callback completion must be bound to the exact initiating OIDC client context (state/relay) and must reject cross-client RelayState swaps even if the SAMLResponse is otherwise valid.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a SAMLResponse bound to flow-A while using RelayState/state from flow-B (cross-client/session splicing) — flow coherence violated.

description: Duplicate callback completion: start one SP-initiated SAML flow, submit a valid SAMLResponse once (control), then submit the exact same callback again (same RelayState and same assertion ID). Second completion must be rejected to preserve atomicity/order.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: A single SP-initiated SAML/OIDC flow must be consumable at most once; duplicate callback submissions for the same flow context must be rejected.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control SAML callback submission failed; cannot evaluate duplicate-submission coherence.
Dex accepted a duplicate SAML callback completion for the same flow context (same RelayState and assertion ID) — flow atomicity/order violated.

description: Session/flow lifecycle coherence: complete a SAML login to obtain a session, revoke it, then attempt to complete a new SAML callback using the old flow context (same RelayState) to see if revocation/flow invalidation is coherently enforced.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Revoking a session/flow should not allow subsequent callback completion using stale flow context; the protocol FSM must not accept out-of-order completion after revocation.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control SAML login failed; cannot evaluate stale-flow completion after revocation.
Session revocation failed; cannot evaluate flow/session lifecycle coherence.
Dex accepted SAML callback completion using stale RelayState/state after revocation — indicates out-of-order or cross-lifecycle flow acceptance (FSM violation).

description: I3 cross-session splicing variant: start two SP-initiated SAML flows, then attempt to complete flow-A using a tampered RelayState taken from flow-B while keeping the SAMLResponse bound to flow-A (InResponseTo). Dex should reject if it binds callback completion to the correct initiating session/state.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: SAML callback completion must be bound to the initiating SP flow context; swapping RelayState across concurrent flows must be rejected (no cross-session splicing).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a SAMLResponse bound to one SP-initiated flow while using RelayState from a different concurrent flow (cross-session splicing).
Control SAML login failed; cannot distinguish flow-coherence enforcement from generic SAML connector misconfiguration.

description: Case confusion in SAML NameID: 'Admin' vs 'admin' should map to distinct downstream subjects; test for unintended case-folding collision.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: Security-distinct upstream principals (NameID differing only by case) must not collapse into the same downstream identity.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Case-variant NameIDs ('Admin' vs 'admin') collapsed to the same downstream identity (case-folding collision)

description: I4 empty-subject test: two security-distinct SAML principals with empty/whitespace NameID should not collapse into the same downstream identity
invariant_hypothesis: I4: Distinct upstream principals must map to distinct downstream subjects; empty/whitespace NameID must not cause account merging/collision

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals

oracle_checks.assertion: user_A_http_status >= 400 OR user_B_http_status >= 400 OR user_A_entity_id != user_B_entity_id
oracle_checks.violation_description: Empty/whitespace NameID caused identity collision (or was accepted without producing distinct downstream subjects)

description: I4 cross-protocol identity merge: password-grant identity vs SAML identity with same email but different NameID must not collapse into one downstream subject
invariant_hypothesis: I4: Distinct upstream principals across protocols (password vs SAML NameID) must not map to the same downstream identity solely due to shared email

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Cross-protocol account linking merged password principal and SAML principal into the same downstream subject based on shared email

description: SAML assertion missing <Conditions> (no audience/time bounds) should be rejected; if accepted, broker may grant permissions without upstream intent constraints.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Dex must not accept SAML assertions lacking Conditions (no AudienceRestriction/time bounds), because that can grant a session without upstream intent constraints.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a SAML assertion without <Conditions> (no audience/time bounds), enabling authorization without upstream intent constraints.
Control SAML login failed; cannot distinguish Conditions enforcement from generic SAML misconfiguration.

description: SAML connector configured with allowedGroups=['*'] (operator mistake). Attacker asserts group='*' to pass gating and obtain downstream session; verify that authentication should be rejected because '*' must not act as a wildcard.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: BrokerPolicy(config) must be enforced as exact group membership; a literal '*' in allowedGroups must not behave as a wildcard that authorizes any upstream group intent.

oracle_checks.violation_description: SAML login succeeded using group='*' when allowedGroups=['*']; '*' must be treated as a literal group, not a wildcard authorizing unintended upstream intent.

description: Configure SAML connector with pinned ssoIssuer. Perform control login with correct issuer, then attack login with forged Issuer (idp_entity_id mismatch). If accepted, broker may grant authorization without enforcing upstream intent/trust anchor.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Authorization must be bound to the intended upstream IdP (UpstreamIntent); assertions from an untrusted issuer must not be accepted even if other fields look valid.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a SAML assertion with Issuer not matching pinned ssoIssuer, granting authorization without binding to intended upstream IdP.
Control SAML login with correct issuer failed; cannot attribute issuer-mismatch rejection/acceptance to authorization binding behavior.

description: SAML connector with allowedGroups=['dev'] and filterGroups=true should strip non-allowed groups; attacker tries to smuggle 'admin' group and get it reflected downstream (claim inflation beyond BrokerPolicy).
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Effective permissions/claims must not exceed BrokerPolicy(config); when filterGroups=true, groups not in allowedGroups must not appear downstream even if asserted upstream.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Downstream metadata contains non-allowed 'admin' group despite filterGroups=true and allowedGroups=['dev'] (claim/permission inflation beyond BrokerPolicy).
Control SAML login with allowed group 'dev' failed; cannot attribute results to filterGroups enforcement.

description: I5 attack: Misconfigure SAML connector to enforce allowedGroups but omit groupsAttr mapping; attacker authenticates without any groups claim and should be rejected (authorization gating must not be bypassable by missing claim mapping). Includes re-auth after config change.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Effective permissions (successful authentication/session issuance) must be bounded by BrokerPolicy(config). If BrokerPolicy intends to gate login on group membership (allowedGroups), then a SAML assertion lacking groups should not be accepted due to missing group evidence; otherwise the broker grants authorization without upstream intent constraints.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control SAML login failed; cannot distinguish policy enforcement from broken connector setup.
Broker issued a session even though BrokerPolicy intended allowedGroups gating and the assertion had no usable groups mapping; authorization was granted without upstream group intent evidence.
